extra: The first stage load reaches this window. Code, map data and any padding still need their exact boundaries.
Second stage payload loaded at $C800. Individual asset boundaries remain to be classified.

comments.text: Advance the active slot's actor type, choose a facing frame by comparing its X coordinate with Arthur and initialize its frame delay. Shift it four pixels up and occasionally select type $13.
On a nonzero scroll phase, advance the current sprite frame. Reaching frame $37 moves the actor down four pixels and switches it to actor type four.
Every eighth value of $BC advance the shape by two. At shape $0E or later, clear the flags and advance the actor type before the common positioning path.
On scroll phase three, move the shape backward by two. Below shape four, deactivate the slot and its linked slot if present, then decrement the optional actor count.
Age the frame delay or jump to the transition for a screen-edge position. Depending on pose flags, move down then sample terrain through $3D15 and $3C29.

The bytes through $88F3 match the stage-three movement handler at the same addresses. The fragment adds horizontal and vertical offsets and contains the start of the next handler. Stage one ends its preceding handler at the jump at $88D7.
The byte immediately before the club name is $12. In the stage-three overlay this address holds the low operand for the store to $19B4.
Thirty-two glyph codes spell WIGAN RUGBY LEAGUE FOOTBALL CLUB. This uses the game's own alphabet with $3E for spaces.
Set shape $52, a counter of four and a delay of $40. Advance the actor type to $2D and continue into its update.
Check actor bounds and take the current facing bit from the shape. Decrement the turn delay and either sample terrain or pick a new facing and delay.
Toggle the shape low bit. Pick one of four turn delays from $18 through $48 in steps of $10.

Sample terrain 21 pixels below the actor, restore the original Y coordinate, then test the resulting map pointer and tile properties. Use the facing bit and the adjacent attributes to choose a horizontal adjustment.
Combine the two phase bits in $BC with base shape $52 and the facing bit. Enter the common hit-counter handler with Y set to two.
Enter the common hit-counter handler with Y set to $0B.

Use the flags to index two step tables. Horizontal movement subtracts the step below shape $9C and adds it from $9C onward. Apply the vertical step and refresh the sprite descriptor operands before checking bounds.
Use the low phase bit to select alternating values for four resident sprite descriptor bytes.
Three horizontal step magnitudes indexed by the active slot's flags.
Three signed vertical step values indexed by the same flags.

Set the IRQ operand at $5D07 to five. Advance the parent to type $2F, give it shape $5F and initialize its horizontal state. Allocate two type $30 slots, save their indexes in $AE and $AF and initialize the pose and delay.

Retire through $3397 if the second linked slot changed type. Check Arthur's proximity from the right before moving the parent. The sign of the horizontal state selects direction. Stop at the movement limit and use shape $60 when stopped.
When both low phase bits are clear, choose a target pose using the random byte and, for index zero, the distance to Arthur. Move $B0 one step toward the target.

Decrement the parent delay. At expiry choose a fresh delay and possible movement direction. Spawn a type $31 projectile if fewer than three slots already hold that type. The pose indexes its initial offsets.
Put both linked slots one pixel right and eight pixels below the parent. Add the pose to $62 and $67 respectively to choose their shapes.
Four pose codes indexed by the phase, with the index reversed when moving right.
Four target pose values for the parent. The updater steps $B0 toward the selected value.
Three distances subtracted from the parent's X for a new projectile.
Three distances added to the parent's Y for a new projectile.

Decrement X and free the slot if the resulting X is at least $AC. Animate shapes $47–$4A. Its signed vertical state selects movement toward Arthur's Y or the limit forty pixels above him. The update can change the vertical state at random.

Move left until X drops below $10, then change to type $24. While onscreen periodically start an animation. Its final phase can drop a type $26 actor, play effect two and change the slot to type seven.
Allocate a slot at the parent position with shape $51 and set its linked slot marker to $FF.
Set a random countdown with bit seven set, switch to type nine and give the slot a counter of two.
Choose the initial facing by comparing X to Arthur. Advance type after the countdown expires and run the common hit check with parameter two.
Advance type when the unsigned difference in Y is below three or at least $FD. Step two pixels toward Arthur and continue into the horizontal update.
Cycle the animation when $BB is zero. Select a horizontal step using the shape facing bit and the phase bit. Free the slot if the result leaves the horizontal limit.
Four signed horizontal steps indexed by facing and phase.
Mark the actor type inactive with $FF.
Advance type and initialize shape $38, countdown $60 and hit counter two.
Age the countdown and run the common hit check while it is active. At expiry reset it and enter the attack phase with hit-check parameter two.
Save the hit-check parameter and previous type, then choose shape $3D and type $1B.
Progress through the attack animation when $BB is zero. On completion restore the old type and spawn three type $1C slots with horizontal steps minus two, zero and plus two.
Set the hit counter, shape and delay. Clear the direction flag before advancing the actor to type $28.
On phase zero choose shape $40 or advance type when that shape is already active. Apply the resident coordinate helpers and check hits with parameter eight.
Animate from $39 and reverse the direction flag at the end of the countdown. Use the actor map pointer, adjacent terrain properties and random tests to decide whether to move or enter another phase.
On phase zero select shape $40, or retire the optional slot when it has reached shape $3F.
Count inactive slots. With at least three, preserve the sign of the direction flag in the delay byte, switch to type $2B and start the shared attack phase.
Recover the direction flag from the delay's sign bit, clear that bit and return to type $29.

Choose shape and horizontal movement from the signed direction byte. Add the vertical speed to the position and increment that speed. Free the projectile at the horizontal limit or if it wraps into the Y interval below $70.
Enter initialization with $FF for the flag. Type $14 enters two bytes later and uses zero instead.
Start at shape $1F with delay $10. Save the original Y coordinate and set type $15.
On countdown expiry advance the actor type and give the jump an initial index of nine.
Apply the vertical step indexed by the countdown. When the initialization flag is negative, an odd $BB skips aging the countdown. After the last step switch type and set the next delay to four.
After the countdown, move up a pixel on each update until the original height is reached. Restore type $15 and set a delay of $1C.
Vertical increments read in descending order from index nine to zero by the type $16 jump.
First 256 bytes copied to $C400 by $53B4. These are title-screen character codes.
Next 256 bytes copy to $C500 through $53BA. The tail is also the source region of the title logo copy.
$53C5 reads 200 entries beginning here. It sets bit 7 before writing them from $C028 through $C0EF.
At column $4B, call $4873 when both flag tests permit it. At coarse scroll value $08, run $2F17 and reinitialize scrolling through $2E4D for selector $01.
At horizontal position $E1 or later, clear the negative flag at $EA when either low bit of $2945 is set. At row $12 and horizontal position $BC or beyond, call $4873 when $E9 is negative.
Write $80 to the property for character one except at row $12 with joystick bit two set, when the value is $20.

In coarse regions seven through nine patch $3678 to JMP, set $5D03 and $945B to $0A and clear the extra sprite work arrays when enabling the draw path. Call the update at $939B when the patch is active.
In coarse region ten, if $945B is $0A, restore RTS at $3678 and write $0C to $5D03 and $945B.
Use the coarse region and scroll offsets to decide whether to call the right-edge actor allocator.
At phase one and coarse region nine or beyond, test whether the confined scrolling loop can run. Otherwise at coarse region eight write the property for character five based on the fine X offset.
While the region, control flags and $EB permit, refresh the scroll and motion paths, wait for the frame tick, copy the current fine scroll to the IRQ operands and rebuild the sprite list.

Require the phase and random gates to pass with fewer than three optional actors. Create type $25 close to Arthur's height when the special case passes and neither $12 nor $25 is active. Otherwise choose a height for type $24. Both start at X=$AC, use shape $47 and increment the optional count.
Clear 32 live flags at $93FB and their 32 X positions at $941B.
Begin at the current phase parity and examine every other entry. For a nonzero X, place its X, Y, colour $0C and shape $8D in the sprite list.

Advance each Y by eight and wrap its range. In coarse regions seven and eight randomly activate new entries. Outside those regions occasionally clear active entries. Move each active X to the left, wrapping past the edge.
Thirty-two activation flags read and written by $939B.
Thirty-two live horizontal positions. Zero skips queueing a sprite in $9374.
Thirty-two vertical positions advanced by eight at $939D and read by the sprite queue at $9383.
Enable and disable marker written beside the resident IRQ operand at $5D03.

Section 00 has 17 ordered spawn records. Each six-byte record contains a 16-bit X tile, a 16-bit Y tile, packed sub-tile offsets and the actor ID. The scan at $30B3 advances after allocating the actor.

Section 01 has 3 ordered spawn records. Each six-byte record contains a 16-bit X tile, a 16-bit Y tile, packed sub-tile offsets and the actor ID. The scan at $30B3 advances after allocating the actor.
Section 00 has 39 optional spawn positions. Each record holds the two tile coordinates and one packed sub-tile byte. The bounded search at $3175 tests visibility and a random condition.
Section 01 has 7 optional spawn positions. Each record holds the two tile coordinates and one packed sub-tile byte. The bounded search at $3175 tests visibility and a random condition.
Three little-endian start addresses for stage 1 music. The resident stage setter copies the six bytes into index six of the SID song table.
Stage 1 supplies this starting address for voice 1 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Stage 1 supplies this starting address for voice 2 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Stage 1 supplies this starting address for voice 3 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Continuation of the stage 1 tune region. Following command targets from its three starting pointers reaches the last phrase bytes at $9D01.

Use the tile code as the index into the $B6 page selected by $2EEF. $48CC subtracts the selected byte from the player's ground-aligned Y value.
Surface offsets for the other terrain bank. $2EEF loads $B7 as the page for the pointer at $C4/$C5.
Tile properties for the first terrain bank. $3C29 maps nearby character-screen positions through this table and stores the attribute bytes at $EE-$F5.
Second terrain bank's tile attributes. $2EEF selects page $B9 for the pointer at $C2/$C3.
The frame hook patches this property in the second terrain bank. Characters two through four keep the values loaded with the stage.
The same frame hook changes this entry at coarse region eight. The rest of the page holds second-bank terrain properties.
Colour lookup by terrain character code. The first bank case in $2EEF selects this page for $4BF8.
Colour lookup by terrain character code. The second bank case in $2EEF patches $4BF8 to this page.

Bottom-right character codes for the lower half of each tile. $505D and $5078 read this page.
Eleven 64-byte VIC sprite slots starting at pointer $20. These slots match in all five stage images and render projectile silhouettes and small circular effects.
Stage sprite slots at pointers $2B through $97. Includes the graveyard enemy poses, weapon silhouettes and large monster fragments. The 64th byte of each slot is outside the 24 by 21 pixel raster.
